artifact.title: AWS announces AWS Interconnect - last mile preview with Equinix
artifact.summary: AWS Interconnect - last mile is now available in preview with Equinix. You can connect your infrastructure across Equinix's global network of 282 data centers worldwide to AWS in a few clicks. Interconnect - last mile gives you managed, private, and resilient connections to AWS, so you don't have to order cross-connects or configure routers. To set up in the AWS Management Console, choose an AWS Region, a bandwidth speed, a Direct Connect gateway, and your Equinix Fabric One project ID. AWS generates an activation key, which you enter in the Equinix Fabric One portal to complete the setup. You can also initiate the connection from the Equinix Fabric One portal. AWS and Equinix set up quad-redundant capacity in advance, across two locations and four separate links, with BGP peering, VLANs and ASNs configured for you. Every connection is built for maximum resilience and comes with a 99.99% availability SLA. Traffic between AWS and Equinix edge devices is encrypted with MACsec by default. During the preview, you can order 1 Gbps Interconnect - last mile connections at no charge to the US West (N. California) Region through the San Jose metro and to the US East (N. Virginia) Region through the Northern Virginia metro. When Interconnect - last mile with Equinix becomes generally available, you'll be able to scale bandwidth from 1 Gbps to 100 Gbps in the console. You can create connections using the console, the AWS CLI, or the API. Partners can integrate using the open API package

artifact.summary: The US data centre development pipeline expanded by 54 GW in the second quarter of 2026, marking a 29% increase year-on-year as developers accelerated construction amid growing concerns over power availability, according to a new report by Wood Mackenzie. The expansion is expected to intensify the focus on electricity supply, grid infrastructure and clean energy procurement as data centres emerge as a major source of incremental power demand in the US. The cumulative disclosed data centre pipeline has crossed 430 GW, with around 59% of the capacity under active development. Nearly 80 GW of projects were under construction, up from 44 GW at the end of the first quarter, Wood Mackenzie said in its US data centre pipeline report. The pipeline added 5% capacity quarter-on-quarter. Meanwhile, utility commitments backed by signed electricity service or construction agreements reached 201 GW, equivalent to 26% of projected US peak electricity demand in 2026. However, the rapid expansion is facing mounting opposition from local communities and lawmakers. artifact.title: Amazon Looks to 960 MW Nuclear Project in Indiana
artifact.summary: X-energy, American Electric Power (AEP), and Amazon have signed a development agreement for a proposed 960 MW small modular reactor facility at the retired Breed Generating Station site in Sullivan County, Indiana. The proposed project would deploy twelve Xe-100 reactors, each rated at 80 MWe. Amazon is providing development funding. The facility remains in feasibility and development, with no construction or commercial operation date announced. The Xe-100 is a Generation IV high-temperature gas-cooled reactor that uses helium coolant and TRISO particle fuel. The multi-unit design could allow phased deployment, subject to site engineering, grid interconnection, environmental review, licensing and financing. The project is intended to add electricity to the regional grid rather than exclusively power an Amazon data center. The Indiana proposal follows Amazon and X-energy’s Cascade advanced nuclear project with Energy Northwest in Washington. X-energy is also developing an initial four-unit deployment for Dow’s Seadrift industrial site in Texas. The Amazon–X-energy collaboration has a broader goal of supporting more than 5 GW of nuclear capacity by 2039; these are development targets rather than operating capacity. In Schneider’s 20-panel comparison, the software-defined configuration required 87% less control wiring, 91% fewer terminals and 85% less copper in the control wiring.
